[b]At the Banks of the Strait[/b]
-
[sub]Erene RP[/sub]]
[i]Sealiph Ibrahim stands on the banks of Argos-Shamat strait on a beach just outside Imdekka, he feels the flow of its waters as it laps over his bare feet, likewise soaking the bottom of his resplendent cape and robe. He thinks little of it, his mind is focused elsewhere. He longed for the council of his old friend and brother Hashim, if only he had not apostatised well into his middle age. And that of his greatest love, Sajidah, who passed on giving him his only son. Perhaps it was a poor idea to remember the losses in his life at this moment, surrounded by his guards, though they remained at a distance, he thought as a tear flowed down his cheek.

Perhaps they would see it as weakness from an aging monarch or perhaps this is how he views himself. He breaks from his reverie as the captain of his guard approaches him, Irman the Stern, Amir Al-Mu'mineen, the sun begins to travel below the sea. Perhaps it is time to return to the palace? Ibrahim cast him aside with the flick of his withered wrist. Permit me to indulge in the feeling of the sun while I still can. He said before continuing after drawing a breath. We shall leave when it sets. Irman prepared to reply but stopped. He would not question his Sealiphs orders this day, not over something this minor.

Sealiph Ibrahim returns to his thoughts this time on that commander Irman the Stern; he was a young man and of his tribe, his sister's son. Perhaps he would succeed him, he thought. Then he thought of the commander's youth, he was young, around 20, perhaps 25? His age was showing, he recalled a recent memory when he went to the Assembly of Governance to hear about some quarrel. As he looked upon the collective of Emirs he noticed their youth. None older than 35. Though he had appointed them, he never looked upon them in their masses. He felt so very old. 

Though he was only 63 and had many more years of life left in him, the duties of governance and conflict aged him. He ached everywhere. Before he could continue his self-pity, Irman the Stern returned to his side. Amir Al-Mu'mineen, the sun has risen its last. It is time to return to the palace. Sealiph Ibrahim thought to protest but as he looked outwards toward the horizon he thought better of it and simply nodded following Irman to the car.

As he sat in the back seat parallel to the Commander, he did not think he simply closed his eyes, awaiting for the drive to be over. He did not feel like having any discussion with Irman or his driver. He began to drift off as he was driven, but every bump in the road made him ache more, his weakness was now on full display, but he stopped caring. Physical pain was expected, he reasoned, not the emotional weakness he had previously put on show. Irman had concernedly turned over to him to see if his Sealiph was alright but was once more waved away. The weakness of age, you shall feel it before long. Ibrahim jokes, giving a warm smile. Irman smiled but did not laugh. In his heart of hearts he knew Ibrahim's time was nearing.

They soon reached Imdekka and then his palace. The driver opened Ibrahim's door and as he tried to get out, the weakness returned, he fell back upon the car seat. He called for Irman to fetch him his cane, which he did with haste, handing it over to Ibrahim. He snatched it and took his first aided step out of the car and slowly but surely into the palace. When he reached his room, it felt cold, he dearly missed his wife. He took no other wife after her passing.

He unclipped his cape and shed his robe, collapsing on the bed still in his silk clothes. He fell asleep, another day had passed and in 8 hours the sun would rise and so would he.[/i][/spoiler]
